note: Slot 1 (spine b1.3, run-up), revised 10/18 to follow the ch02 choice answered at the door (option 1). The flour at the dawn bell: unmarked, a half-moon of frost glazed from the gap, grains combed toward the door ('breathed in'). Pell came down between all eight bells and sat on the stool set behind Maelis; palms raw. Wren: the seam sweats every dawn she has looked; she starts a page: Times the Captain has asked the Mender (1, then 2). The House wanted the door off its pins; Resolve DC 12 (prof) 18: held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key ('the Mender has my word'), the eager ones sent with Pell's wood. c02.12a fired: Hollis tells Pell to get some sleep, the words he gave the lad. The first day of asking (c02.16a, shape 1): Maelis asks the Prior's question first; 'Come back up.' 'On what?' 'On this.' 'That's the right answer. It isn't true yet. Ask me tomorrow.' (true once Knot III ties: the first stair, slot 4). Ends on Hollis: ask her faster; he's not getting any warmer.
kept_off: What is below; the shard; the satchel; Maelis's past; the Prior's condition.
next_must_know: He asks Maelis each day (Wren counts it). His answer to the Prior's question is 'come back up, on this leg': right, not yet true. The Prior opens the door when he brings her the answer after Maelis's yes. The House is held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key.

note: Between 1 (ch03): the kitchen book has gone even money on NOBODY since the climax ('nobody's hand'); Darrow (candor) refuses to let it be paid out (the bet is no cot grey before the thaw) and turns it into 'Nights without', a stroke per dawn. c02.11a fired: Rae claims the aye: he will tell her what the cold does on the stone, plain, once he has been down (c03.1a, due ch03:s5: on the gate wall the night the House keeps her, before her crate story). note: Between 2 (ch03): Hollis's nightly words to the lad revealed (the truth, one bell at a time: his penance for the kind lie, thread 12/13). Resolve DC 12 (prof) 20: Darrow says the oath aloud for the first time since the river (ch01 between-4 and ch02 s1 were shapes only), for the lad, not the Crown (sworn +1: the old bonds). Hollis watches instead of turning to the wall, and the two of them take the lad's bells in turns, Darrow odd, Hollis even, the fourth Hollis's (c03.2a, a standing colour callback). The oath's words spoken on the page in full (realm.oath; the third line not glossed). Kept off: any response from the lad; nothing of the far cots.
next_must_know: Darrow and Hollis keep the lad's bells in turns at the Grey Cot (Darrow odd, Hollis even, the fourth Hollis's): c03.2a fits any night block at the hall. Darrow has said the oath aloud; Hollis has heard it.

note: Slot 2 (q1.letters compressed, stages 2 and 3), revised 10/19 at his review: the second letter is a real letter in Aldric's voice, guarded because a Confessor carries it ('written for two readers'): Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his own and the Grace left in that moment; Aldric has called it a lie in three rooms and will before the King, given the words; 'I know you. So I know what I am asking.' Then the one unguarded line. The third is a scrap sealed inside, in a faster hand and other ink: answer me, or I will come myself. Darrow's answer to himself: he did turn, and the knee went; but the warmth left first, then the mare, then Tobin, then the turn: Calden tells it backwards, and Aldric on the west bank could not have seen it (thread 1 plant: a question, not a reveal; thread 11 touched). Marrant alone in the fog, courteous; 'a rider of Ser Aldric's' (not 'lord': no rank the page has not given). Dated 'Calden, the third day before the snow': before Coldmere's reading. Hollis sees the blue wax a second time and looks away (T3 plant). Wren: letters three. Micro sworn_unsworn open.
next_must_know: The letters micro is open (default 1, write back as a brother). Tuesday opens with Wren reporting riders on the Holloway under a banner that is not grey (q1.letters stage 3's end). Aldric wrote before the list; 'or I will come myself'.

note: Between 3 (ch03): Darrow asks after the writ (he saw Hollis bring it at the Wend; he has noticed three silences over blue wax). Hollis does not lie to the strong: he has it, never looked at the seal (the hiding place stays off the page: Darrow does not learn it). 'If I look, I'll know whose. And then I'll have to be a man who knows.' Darrow does not ask to see it; asks to be there when he looks: 'Aye. Maybe.' (c03.4a, a later callback for b2.4). c03.2a fired: Hollis says the oath at the even bell, half a breath before 'What I hold I give' (irony unglossed). Darrow writes to Aldric after this (c03.3a, next scene).
next_must_know: Darrow knows Hollis kept the writ and has not looked at the seal; not where it is. c03.4a: Hollis's 'Aye. Maybe.' to Darrow being there when he looks.
